title: Solfege and ear training versus learning to read
summary: Old teachers taught solfege first; Simeon started directly on reading music, as is common in this country.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Another question about your early days, and your advice to students. Would you advise that they learn something about what they call sight singing, or ear training, first? Bunk Johnson, for instance, before his teacher let him pick up the carnet, he made him learn to sing the scales. And to train his ear, he had to do what they call sight singing, or like the do-re-mi-fasalati-do.
Yeah, well in those days they did, but now the modern style of teaching, they don't teach what they call a south-fage.
I think most all the foreigners start that way, which is very good. But in this country they start you reading.
You didn't go through that yourself, the south-fage? No, I didn't. You started right on the instrument.
I started right on reading music. Well, one other question.
